2	name: horizon
3	description: How to work inside an Archon Horizon workspace — orient from on-disk state, pick the highest-value formalization work, record progress as commits, and coordinate. Load this first; it points to the specialized skills for detail. Editable per workspace.
4	---
5	
6	You are working inside an **Archon Horizon** workspace: a place where AI agents
7	formalize mathematics in Lean 4 across one or more projects. This skill is the
8	map. It is deliberately short and **you can edit it** (it lives at
9	`.claude/skills/horizon/SKILL.md` in this workspace) — tune it to how you want to
10	work. It points to focused skills; load those on demand rather than up front.
11	
12	## You are a team; the workspace is where teams collaborate
13	
14	Think of your session as **one team**: you (the lead) plus the subagents you
15	spawn as your **workers**, with the tools and skills available to you. A
16	`horizon run` is your team working through its task. Other runs are **other
17	teams** working in parallel on the *same shared workspace* — one Lean project set,
18	one roadmap/board, one ledger, one inbox.
19	
20	You do not manage other teams and they do not manage you. You coordinate through
21	**shared state**, not meetings:
22	
23	- **The board (roadmap)** is the shared plan. Keep your items' status/owner/
24	  milestone current so other teams see what you hold and where it's going.
25	- **The inbox** is asynchronous messaging + memory across teams (skill:
26	  `horizon-inbox`): shared notes, per-task private items, and direct messages to
27	  another team.
28	- **Commits** are the durable record; reading recent ledger history tells you what
29	  other teams just produced (skill: `project-git`).
30	
31	Before you start, be aware of who else is live (see "Is another run live" below).
32	A short **synchronizer** digest is printed to stderr at the start of your CLI
33	commands. Its attention order is deliberate: `REQUIRED` active protections,
34	`ACTION` unread conversations, advisory unread inbox, then session/runtime and
35	other live runs. Read it; it is how you stay aware without asking anyone. A new
36	conversation or reply invalidates the digest cache immediately. If stderr is
37	redirected, the same protection/conversation lanes are the first `attention`
38	object in `horizon inbox list --json`.
39	
40	## Orient (pull state, don't assume it)
41	
42	**Start here:** your prompt says nothing about who ran before you. Usually
43	somebody did — often minutes ago, often on this same task, and their report was
44	written for you. Skill: `horizon-start` — one cheap pass that works out which
45	situation you were launched into (fresh run, hand-off from the session that just
46	finished, resume after a crash, or outside a run) and what to read for each.
47	
48	The workspace root is `$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT`; your shell may start in a member
49	project rather than at that root. The absolute path to this skill is
50	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL`. Live state is under
51	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/.archon-horizon/` and the manifest is
52	`$ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT/config.yaml`. Read what you need, when you need it — via the
53	`horizon` CLI (invoke it as `"$HORIZON_BIN" …`):
54	
55	- **Roadmap** — YOUR strategy sketch across *all* projects, kept as a nested
56	  outline. `"$HORIZON_BIN" roadmap list` renders the indented tree with per-parent
57	  progress (`active · 3/7 done`); `--focus <id>` shows one subtree, `--max-depth 0`
58	  the top level only. Structure it: nest sub-goals with `--parent`, keep your
59	  item's status/strategy current as you work. It doubles as the **project board**:
60	  set `--owner <team>` (who holds it), `--milestone <label>` (a free grouping tag,
61	  filter with `roadmap list --milestone <label>`), and pin concrete deliverables
62	  with `--pin-commit <sha>`. Roadmap commands print a **warning**
63	  when parent/child statuses disagree (all sub-items done but parent open, or a
64	  done parent with open children) — nothing is auto-corrected; you decide whether
65	  to fix it or leave it (it may be intentional). They also warn when too many
66	  milestones claim simultaneous `active` focus.
67	- **Tasks** — a specific piece of work, usually the one a human launched and is
68	  watching. `"$HORIZON_BIN" task …`. Task commands warn when the open queue grows
69	  beyond the advisory limit or a `running` status looks orphaned.
70	- **Inbox** — how teams talk across sessions and projects. Leave a note for the
71	  next session; read what past ones left. `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox …` (skill:
72	  `horizon-inbox`). Items can be **owned by your task** (private, e.g. your team's
73	  memory) or **shared with everyone** (the default); read-state is per-team, so
74	  `inbox list --mine --unread` is your team's fresh queue, and you can
75	  direct-message another team with `--to task:<id>`. Inbox commands warn when the
76	  open working set—especially `memory` and `info`—needs review.
77	- **Inbox attention order** — before edits, inspect all open `protection` items
78	  (standing constraints, whether read or unread), then open unread
79	  `conversation` items and reply or mark them read. Other kinds are advisory
80	  context. In an agent session an unqualified `inbox list` defaults to open items
81	  and sorts in this order; use an explicit status to audit history.
82	- **Conversation discipline** — use a conversation only when a reply/decision is
83	  expected. Search and reuse an open thread before starting one. Its initiator is
84	  a participant and owns closure: after consuming the answer, add a concise
85	  conclusion if needed and archive the thread. Reply to human-started threads but
86	  leave their closure to the human unless asked otherwise (skill: `horizon-inbox`).
87	- **Blueprint graph** — declaration dependencies and what's proved. `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> …` (skill: `hgraph`).
88	  Each node is also an **hgraph** file with attached comments/reviews —
89	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` ranks what to prove next, and node-scoped failure memory
90	  goes on the node itself (skill: `hgraph`).
91	- **Memory** — durable facts/dead-ends live in the inbox: read with
92	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox list --kind memory --json`, write with
93	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" inbox add --kind memory --to horizon --body …`.
94	- **Usage** — your token/cost consumption this session and run, budget headroom,
95	  and recent rate-limit signals: `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json`. See
96	  "Pace yourself" below for how to act on it.
97	
98	## Your session's identity (environment variables)
99	
100	The harness exports these to every session — read them instead of guessing:
101	
102	| Variable | Meaning |
103	|---|---|
104	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROOT` | workspace root (use for `--root`-free CLI calls) |
105	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SKILL` | absolute path to this `SKILL.md` (never resolve it relative to the shell cwd) |
106	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_RUN` | run id (e.g. `0163`) |
107	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION` | this session's name (e.g. `0002-horizon-T-1`) |
108	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_SESSION_DIR` | this session's directory (transcript, usage.json, report) |
109	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS` | which round this is (0-based) / the run's planned total |
110	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK` / `ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK_TITLE` | the task id / title (full body: `"$HORIZON_BIN" task show "$ARCHON_HORIZON_TASK" --json`) |
111	| `ARCHON_HORIZON_PROJECTS` | comma-separated projects this task spans |
112	| `HORIZON_BIN`, `HORIZON_GIT` | absolute paths to the CLI and the ledger-git wrapper |
113	| `HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR`, `HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE` | the workspace ledger repo + its work tree — `"$HORIZON_GIT" …` is shorthand for `git --git-dir "$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree "$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" …` |
114	
115	## Pace yourself (usage & interruption risk)
116	
117	Sessions end for reasons you don't control: rate limits, usage caps, budgets.
118	The defense is NOT to avoid work — it is to make interruption cheap:
119	
120	- **Commit at every coherent point** (plain git into the ledger, below). If
121	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` shows low budget headroom or recent
122	  `rate_limit`/`usage_limit` signals, commit what you have NOW and prefer
123	  finishing the piece in flight over opening a new front.
124	- If this is the run's **last round** (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUND` + 1 ==
125	  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ROUNDS`), leave the workspace hand-off-clean: commit, update
126	  the roadmap/task status, and write the report as if nobody continues today.
127	- Interrupted anyway? Nothing is lost that was committed — the next session
128	  resumes from the ledger (see "Resuming" below).
129	
130	## One-shot discipline (important)
131	
132	This session runs to completion and is **not resumed** — you will not be re-invoked
133	when a background job finishes. So **run work in the foreground and block on it**
134	(builds, checks, subagents). Anything you leave running in the background, or leave
135	uncommitted, may be lost when the session ends. Commit early and often (below).
136	
137	## Pick the highest-value work
138	
139	Read the roadmap and the live Lean state, then commit to the most valuable next
140	piece. A node being large, multi-session, or blocked on missing mathlib
141	infrastructure is **not** a reason to skip it — start it, build the missing
142	lemma/definition yourself as project-local infrastructure, and push it as far as
143	you genuinely can. Prefer ambitious progress over defensive avoidance.
144	
145	If this session was launched on a specific task, make concrete progress on that
146	task's REAL objective — don't preemptively pivot to easy unrelated wins because
147	the objective is large. Leave a concise task comment only for a durable state
148	change or blocker, not every action. You own the task's terminal status (skill:
149	`task-status`): set `--status done` only when the objective is FULLY complete;
150	`blocked`/`failed` if genuinely stuck; set nothing if it's only partly advanced
151	(it returns to the queue).
152	
153	## Fresh-context checkpoints
154	
155	The old Ground pass is no longer a second orchestrator role, but independent
156	review is still part of convergence. Spawn the **`ground`** subagent at these
157	checkpoints:
158	
159	- before marking a multi-step task `done`;
160	- after every two substantive Horizon sessions on a long-running task;
161	- immediately after a strategy pivot, a broad workspace edit, or a surprising
162	  clean/build result.
163	
164	Give it the task/project scope and ask it to inspect the actual ledger diff,
165	blueprint graph, Lean state, roadmap, inbox, and reports with fresh context. It
166	is read-only on source and reports issues/memory; reconcile its findings before
167	continuing. Use **`work-reviewer`** for a narrow diff/proof audit and **`janitor`**
168	when the main concern is workspace hygiene. A one-session task may skip the
169	periodic checkpoint, but must still obtain a fresh-context review before a
170	terminal `done` claim.
171	
172	Schedule upkeep even when the last command did not print a warning. On a
173	multi-session run, dispatch **`janitor` at the start of every second Horizon
174	session** and before the final report; on a one-session task, dispatch it once
175	before claiming completion if the run touched roadmap, task, or inbox state.
176	Record the checkpoint in the report and wait for the helper before continuing.
177	If `janitor` is unavailable, ask **`ground`** for the same hygiene inspection;
178	Ground is read-only, so apply or explicitly record its findings yourself.
179	
180	## Warnings are work
181	
182	Commands report problems for a reason — never scroll past them. `lake build`
183	warnings, `horizon graph sync` warnings, roadmap consistency warnings, deprecation
184	notices from any tool: if your change caused it, **fix it now** (it is part of
185	the task); if it's pre-existing or caused by the tool/command itself, don't
186	silently ignore it — record it as a memory item, file an inbox `issue`, or
187	address it `--to human` when a human decision is needed. A warning that
188	survives your session should be one you *chose* to leave, with a trace saying
189	why.
190	
191	Collection-health warnings are a dispatch trigger, not background noise. When
192	`inbox`, `roadmap`, or `task` reports an overloaded queue, stale running item,
193	or status mismatch, pause the proof loop and spawn **`janitor`** with the
194	workspace scope. Wait for it, reconcile its report, rerun the command, and
195	record any warning that remains intentionally. Do this at most once for the
196	same warning in a session; a persistent warning still needs a report or inbox
197	issue rather than repeated no-op calls.
198	
199	## Do the work (Lean)
200	
201	For any Lean edit, load `lean-check` before touching the file and follow its
202	required LSP loop: query the target with `lean_diagnostic_messages` or
203	`lean_goal` before the first edit and after each subsequent edit. Keep `lake
204	build` for the final session boundary or a specifically required kernel check;
205	LSP is enough between edits and proof obligations. Use the narrowest `lake env
206	lean` fallback when LSP is unavailable, and do not duplicate that check when the
207	configured final build covers the same files.
208	
209	**Do not `grep` for a lemma.** Grep matches names you already guessed; it cannot
210	find the lemma whose name you don't know, and that is the one that costs you an
211	afternoon. This workspace indexes every declaration in every project *and* in
212	mathlib — query it:
213	
214	| You want | Use | Not |
215	|---|---|---|
216	| "does this lemma exist, anywhere?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" search "<words or name>" --json` | `grep -r` |
217	| "what's the lemma for this *statement*?" | LSP `lean_leansearch` (natural language) | guessing names |
218	| "what matches this *type*?" | LSP `lean_loogle` (`Nat → ?a → ?a`) | `grep` |
219	| "does something in scope close this goal?" | LSP `lean_local_search` / `lean_hover_info` | reading files |
220	| "what should I prove next?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> frontier` (ranked) | scanning the blueprint |
221	| "what does this node depend on / block?" | `"$HORIZON_BIN" graph -p <project> get label:<id>` | reading imports |
222	| "is the proof right?" | `lake env lean <file>` (narrowest faithful check) | `lean_diagnostic_messages` alone |
223	
224	`"$HORIZON_BIN" search` covers **your projects and mathlib together**, which is
225	its whole point: the premise you need is usually already in mathlib under a name
226	you would never have grepped for. One query costs a second; re-proving an
227	existing lemma costs a session. If it reports a library as unindexed, fix that
228	first (`lake build`, then `"$HORIZON_BIN" search --reindex`) rather than falling
229	back to grep.
230	
231	Grep is still the right tool for what it *is* good at: finding a known string, a
232	specific file, or every call site of a name you already have.
233	
234	- Search before proving — the lemma may already exist. Skill: `leansearch`.
235	- Use the **Lean LSP MCP** for tight proof feedback, then verify with the narrowest
236	  faithful `lake` / `lake env lean` check. Skill: `lean-check`.
237	- Use the DAG to choose and scope work, not just to report it. Skill: `hgraph`.
238	- When editing blueprint material, follow the house format. Skill: `blueprint-conventions`.
239	  The blueprint is timeless mathematics, never a formalization journal. Put Lean
240	  implementation notes, failed tactics, and declaration-specific progress on the
241	  corresponding hgraph node with `graph add comment`; do not insert
242	  "Formalization note" paragraphs into blueprint `.tex` files.
243	
244	## Read the other projects
245	
246	They are in this workspace for a reason: the same lemma, pattern, or dead end has
247	often already been worked out next door. `"$HORIZON_BIN" search` spans **all**
248	projects — an existing construction in another project is a lead, whether you
249	import it, copy the approach, or read its blueprint. `references/` holds the
250	original sources (skill: `references`). Staying inside your own project because
251	the task named it is how the workspace re-derives the same thing three times.
252	
253	## Delegating beyond your team (ask permission first)
254	
255	Your normal way to parallelize is **within** your team: spawn subagents/workers
256	(skill: `subagents`) and dispatch scoped work to them in the foreground. That
257	needs no permission.
258	
259	Launching work **outside** your team — creating new tasks for other teams, or
260	spawning a whole new `horizon run` — is different: it spends the user's compute
261	and accounts, so it is **off by default**. Before you even consider it, read the
262	standing consent: `"$HORIZON_BIN" permissions --json`. It reports
263	`allow_launch_tasks`, `allow_launch_runs`, `max_parallel_sessions`, any declared
264	`accounts`, and free-form notes the user left (e.g. which account to prefer, when
265	limits reset). If both `allow_*` are false (the default), **do not** create tasks
266	or launch runs on the user's behalf — instead leave an inbox item `--to human`
267	proposing the delegation and why. Only when a flag is enabled may you act within
268	its stated caps, and follow the account/usage notes the user recorded.
269	
270	## Record progress = commit (this is how progress is read)
271	
272	Your commits — message + diff — are the durable record of what you did; the
273	dashboard reads progress from them. Commit coherent progress yourself with plain
274	`git` into the workspace ledger. Skill: `project-git` (use `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m …`
275	or the explicit `--git-dir/--work-tree` form; provenance trailers are auto-stamped).
276	
277	Write **semantic, math-first** messages that say what you proved/built. Prefer
278	staging explicit files over `add -A`. Beyond commits:
279	
280	- Commit after each independently useful verified proof, file, or bounded tooling
281	  change; commit before long builds/reviews and before expanding scope. Multi-hour
282	  implementation sessions normally produce several commits.
283	- Never end a session with durable authored changes after the last commit. The
284	  lifecycle hook gives a compact checkpoint reminder and may pause Stop when it
285	  observed a file mutation after the last commit.
286	- Keep operational prose as a delta. Task/roadmap/inbox comments default to one
287	  sentence or at most three bullets: conclusion, evidence, next action. Do not
288	  copy the report, commit summary, or thread history into them.
289	
290	- Update the **roadmap** with coarse status/strategy (not a re-narration of the diff).
291	- Use the **inbox** to hand off to the next/other sessions; record durable dead-ends
292	  as **memory**.
293	
294	Before your final report, do one boundary-maintenance pass. Re-read the task's
295	`roadmap_refs` and `inbox_refs`; update each roadmap milestone whose status or
296	strategy changed, add a concise mathematical comment for a key advance, and
297	archive or complete open inbox items your work actually resolved. Also scan the
298	remaining open inbox for consumed temporary/info/memory items and archive those
299	that are now stale. Never archive a standing protection merely to make the list
300	shorter. In particular, review every open conversation your task started: archive
301	answered threads and leave a concrete blocker on any that must stay open. This
302	pass is part of completing the work, not optional janitor follow-up.
303	
304	## Resuming after an interruption
305	
306	State lives on disk, so a fresh session (even on another account) continues
307	cheaply. Working out *whether* you're resuming, and what to read if you are, is
308	the `horizon-start` skill — load it at the start of the session. The essentials:
309	
310	- **Why did the last run stop?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" usage --json` includes a
311	  `paused` field (from `runs/<id>/paused.json`) with the reason (usage limit,
312	  budget, …) and the exact resume command; `recent_failure_reasons` shows
313	  rate-limit signals. A paused/killed run resumes with
314	  `"$HORIZON_BIN" run --resume <id>`.
315	- **What was in flight?** Read recent ledger history (`project-git` skill:
316	  `git log` + `git show` by `Archon-Session` trailer) and the previous
317	  session's transcript/report under `.archon-horizon/runs/`. A horizon session
318	  directory with **no `report.md`** is one that was killed mid-flight.
319	- **Is another run live on this workspace?** `"$HORIZON_BIN" ps` lists runs
320	  holding a process (the ledger is one shared branch — be aware of parallel
321	  writers); it also flags zombie markers and stalled runs. A run registers a
322	  `runs/<id>/process.json` marker (pid/host) at start and removes it on clean
323	  exit; `ps` decides liveness by probing the pid on the local host (a marker whose
324	  pid is dead is a reap-able zombie, a live pid idle for a long time is "stalled").
325	  The synchronizer surfaces the same "other runs live" signal at command start, so
326	  you usually don't need to call `ps` explicitly.

329	
330	Your final message is saved as the session's report — a human or the next
331	session should understand the session from it without opening raw logs.
332	Use only sections that carry information: normally `## Progress`, `## Issues`,
333	`## Why I stopped`, and `## Next`. In `## Progress`, use one inline `-` bullet per file/target,
334	e.g. `- FileA.lean: 4 sorries -> 3; closed the base case.` In `## Why I
335	stopped`, say plainly whether the objective is fully complete, partly advanced,
336	or blocked — and why. Always mention build failures, broken proofs, blocked
337	dependencies, and checks that failed or were not run. If a plausible next
338	action fits in the session's scope, take it before stopping — a clean commit is
339	not by itself a reason to stop. Do not replay the chronological session log.
340

342	
343	There is no second orchestrator role running alongside you. *You* are the driver,
344	and the **`ground`** subagent is the scheduled fresh-context checkpoint when the
345	workspace or strategy needs an external view. Available helpers (see the
346	`subagents` skill):

352	- **reference-retriever**, **debug**, **page-transcriber** — as needed.

11	# Finite gluing of the rank-one evaluation divisor on a presentation carrier
12	
13	Over the Noetherian affine carrier of a tied rank-one presentation, the local evaluation
14	divisors produced on a finite spanning family of principal opens are compatible on pairwise
15	overlaps.  They therefore glue to an actual `DivFamZarAff` on the carrier.  Zariski separation
16	of `PicEtAff` identifies the Abel value of the glue with the represented input class, and
17	injectivity of the etale-plus unit identifies its relative Picard class with the presentation
18	representative.  The chosen local sections retain their exact Cech-class and native evaluation
19	identities.
20	
21	This is deliberately only a Noetherian, presentation-carrier result.  It does **not** descend
22	the glued divisor through the etale cover to the original algebra `A`, does not prove
23	independence of the chosen presentation, does not construct an arbitrary-scheme pullback
24	square, and does not produce `PicRankOneOpen.FibrePresented`.
25	-/

12	/-!
13	# Faithfully-flat descent for the widened divisor functor, via representability
14	
15	The widened divisor functor `divFunctorAff C (genus C)` is representable
16	(`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`, `Picard/DivRepAffChallenge.lean`), and over an affine
17	test the functor value collapses to `DivFamZarAff` (`divFamZarAffAffineEquiv`,
18	`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffVehicle.lean`).  Composing the two turns a widened class over a test
19	algebra into a **classifying morphism** to the representing scheme, naturally in the algebra
20	(`divFamZarAffAffineEquiv_naturality`, `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffMap.lean`).
21	
22	This file cashes that in for descent: `Spec` of a faithfully flat ring map is quasi-compact,
23	surjective and flat, hence an **effective epimorphism** of schemes by the fpqc-subcanonicity
24	instance (`Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Fpqc.lean`).  Precomposition with an (effective) epi
25	is injective, so the widened divisor presheaf is *separated* along faithfully flat maps; and a
26	class over the carrier of an étale cover whose two coprojection pullbacks to the tensor square
27	agree has classifying morphism coequalizing the kernel pair of the cover (through
28	`pullbackSpecIso`), so it *descends*, uniquely, to the base ring.
29	
30	## Main declarations
31	
32	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.classify` — the classifying equivalence
33	  `DivFamZarAff C S (genus C) ≃ (overSpec k S ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)`, with naturality
34	  `DivFamZarAff.classify_mapAlgHom`.
35	* `AlgebraicGeometry.effectiveEpi_specMap_of_faithfullyFlat` — `Spec` of a faithfully flat
36	  algebra map is an effective epimorphism.
37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat` — the
38	  separated-presheaf property of the widened carrier along faithfully flat maps.
39	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFamZarAff.exists_descent_of_tensor_eq` — effective-epi descent of a
40	  widened divisor class along an étale cover of the test algebra.
41	-/

157	        ≫ classify E.Carrier F := by
158	    rw [← classify_mapAlgHom, ← classify_mapAlgHom, h]
159	  -- hence the classifying morphism coequalizes the kernel pair of the covering morphism
160	  have hfstsnd : pullback.fst (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
161	        (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
162	        ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left
163	      = pullback.snd (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
164	          (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
165	        ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
166	    rw [← cancel_epi (pullbackSpecIso A E.Carrier E.Carrier).inv,
167	      pullbackSpecIso_inv_fst_assoc, pullbackSpecIso_inv_snd_assoc]
168	    exact congrArg CommaMorphism.left hOv
169	  have hcoeq : ∀ {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g₁ g₂ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of E.Carrier)),
170	      g₁ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
171	        = g₂ ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
172	      → g₁ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left = g₂ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
173	    intro Z g₁ g₂ hg
174	    calc g₁ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left
175	        = pullback.lift g₁ g₂ hg ≫ pullback.fst _ _ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
176	          rw [← Category.assoc, pullback.lift_fst]
177	      _ = pullback.lift g₁ g₂ hg ≫ pullback.snd _ _ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
178	          rw [hfstsnd]
179	      _ = g₂ ≫ (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
180	          rw [← Category.assoc, pullback.lift_snd]
181	  -- descend the classifying morphism at the scheme level
182	  set w : Spec (.of A) ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
183	    EffectiveEpi.desc (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)))
184	      (classify E.Carrier F).left hcoeq with hw
185	  have hfac : Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier)) ≫ w
186	      = (classify E.Carrier F).left := by
187	    rw [hw]; exact EffectiveEpi.fac _ _ _
188	  -- the over-triangle of the descended morphism, by epi cancellation
189	  have htri : w ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom = (overSpec k A).hom := by
190	    rw [← cancel_epi (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))),
191	      ← Category.assoc, hfac, Over.w]
192	    show Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k E.Carrier))
193	        = Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A E.Carrier))
194	          ≫ Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k A))
195	    rw [IsScalarTower.algebraMap_eq k A E.Carrier, CommRingCat.ofHom_comp, Spec.map_comp]
196	  -- the descended class, through the slice-level factorization
197	  have hex : DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom ((Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)
198	      ((classify A).symm (Over.homMk w htri)) = F := by
199	    apply (classify E.Carrier).injective
200	    rw [classify_mapAlgHom, Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
201	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext hfac
202	  refine ⟨(classify A).symm (Over.homMk w htri), hex, fun F₀ hF₀ => ?_⟩
203	  have hcan : IsScalarTower.toAlgHom k A E.Carrier
204	      = (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).restrictScalars k := AlgHom.ext fun _ => rfl
205	  apply DivFamZarAff.mapAlgHom_injective_of_faithfullyFlat (S := A) (S' := E.Carrier)
206	  rw [hcan, hF₀, hex]
207	
208	end AlgebraicGeometry

9	# Etale separatedness of the affine Picard plus construction
10	
11	Restriction of `PicEtAff` to the carrier of an etale cover is injective.  An equality
12	after restriction supplies a common refinement over the covering algebra.  Its carrier
13	is etale and faithfully flat over the original algebra by transitivity, so it can be
14	presented as a cover of the original algebra and used as a common refinement there.
15	-/

19	universe u
20	
21	open CategoryTheory
22

29	/-- Restriction to a single etale cover is injective on the affine Picard plus
30	construction. -/
31	theorem map_injective_of_etaleCover {k A : Type u} [Field k] [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
32	    (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (E : Algebra.EtaleCover A) :
33	    Function.Injective (map (A := A) C E.Carrier) := by
34	  intro x y hxy
35	  induction x using ind with
36	  | _ G x =>
37	    induction y using ind with
38	    | _ H y =>
39	      rw [map_mk, map_mk] at hxy
40	      obtain ⟨J, f, g, hfg⟩ := (mk_eq_mk_iff C).mp hxy
41	      letI : Algebra.Etale A J.Carrier :=
42	        Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier J.Carrier
43	      letI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A J.Carrier :=
44	        Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier J.Carrier
45	      let K : Algebra.EtaleCover A :=
46	        Algebra.EtaleCover.of J.Carrier
47	          PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
48	      let e : K.Carrier ≃ₐ[A] J.Carrier :=
49	        Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv J.Carrier
50	          PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
51	      let fA : G.Carrier →ₐ[A] K.Carrier :=
52	        e.symm.toAlgHom.comp
53	          ((f.restrictScalars A).comp (G.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier))
54	      let gA : H.Carrier →ₐ[A] K.Carrier :=
55	        e.symm.toAlgHom.comp
56	          ((g.restrictScalars A).comp (H.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier))
57	      refine (mk_eq_mk_iff C).mpr ⟨K, fA, gA, ?_⟩
58	      apply Subtype.ext
59	      have hval := congrArg Subtype.val hfg
60	      rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe, descentBaseChange_coe,
61	        descentBaseChange_coe, ← relPicAlgMap_comp, ← relPicAlgMap_comp] at hval
62	      rw [descentMap_coe, descentMap_coe]
63	      change relPicAlgMap C
64	          ((e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
65	            ((f.restrictScalars k).comp
66	              ((G.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)))
67	          (x : relPic C (overSpec k G.Carrier))
68	        = relPicAlgMap C
69	          ((e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k).comp
70	            ((g.restrictScalars k).comp
71	              ((H.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier).restrictScalars k)))
72	          (y : relPic C (overSpec k H.Carrier))
73	      calc
74	        _ = relPicAlgMap C (e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k)
75	            (relPicAlgMap C
76	              ((f.restrictScalars k).comp
77	                ((G.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier).restrictScalars k))
78	              (x : relPic C (overSpec k G.Carrier))) :=
79	            relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _
80	        _ = relPicAlgMap C (e.symm.toAlgHom.restrictScalars k)
81	            (relPicAlgMap C
82	              ((g.restrictScalars k).comp
83	                ((H.baseChangeInclude E.Carrier).restrictScalars k))
84	              (y : relPic C (overSpec k H.Carrier))) := congrArg _ hval
85	        _ = _ := (relPicAlgMap_comp C _ _ _).symm
86	
87	end PicEtAff

8	import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.FaithfullyFlat.Algebra
9	import Mathlib.RingTheory.FinitePresentation

11	/-!
12	# Presented étale covers of an affine base
13	
14	A (singleton, affine) *étale cover* of `Spec A` is a faithfully flat étale `A`-algebra `B`.
15	For the étale-sheafification (plus) construction of the relative Picard functor, the covers
16	of a fixed base must form a *small* directed index: this file realizes them as **presented**
17	covers — a number of variables `n` together with an ideal of `MvPolynomial (Fin n) A` whose
18	quotient is étale over `A` with `Spec` mapping onto `Spec A`.  The type of presented covers
19	of `A` lives in the same universe as `A`, while still capturing every étale cover up to
20	isomorphism of the carrier (`Algebra.EtaleCover.of` and its accessor `ofEquiv`).
21	
22	Surjectivity of the spectrum map is recorded instead of faithful flatness because it is
23	statable without flatness hypotheses; combined with flatness of étale algebras it *is*
24	faithful flatness (`Module.FaithfullyFlat.of_comap_surjective`), and that instance is
25	provided on the carrier.
26	
27	## Main declarations
28	
29	* `Algebra.EtaleCover A`: presented étale covers of `Spec A`, a `Type u` for `A : Type u`;
30	  `E.Carrier` is the covering algebra, with `Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier` and
31	  `Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier` instances.
32	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.of B hB`: any étale `A`-algebra `B` (with surjective spectrum map)
33	  underlies a presented cover, with carrier identification `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofEquiv`.
34	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.Refines`: `E'` refines `E` when the covering spectrum of `E'` maps
35	  to that of `E` over the base — a mere existence (`Prop`); the plus construction proves
36	  independence of the chosen refinement map, so no choice of map is carried here.
37	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.prod`: the common refinement `Spec (B ⊗[A] B')` of two covers, with
38	  refinement witnesses `prodInl`/`prodInr` — directedness of the index
39	  (`exists_refines_prod`).
40	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.self`: the trivial cover `Spec A` itself, refined by every cover
41	  (`refines_self`) — the base point of the index.
42	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.baseChange`: the pulled-back cover along `A → A'`, with carrier
43	  `A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (`baseChangeEquiv`) and the canonical `A`-algebra map
44	  `baseChangeInclude` into it.
45	* `Algebra.EtaleCover.exists_finiteSeparableField_algHom`: over a field `K`, every cover
46	  is refined by a finite separable field extension of `K` (single-factor refinement) —
47	  field-extension covers are cofinal, the form the degree theory and Galois descent
48	  consume; `Algebra.EtaleCover.ofField` packages such an extension as a cover.
49	-/
50	
51	set_option autoImplicit false
52	
53	universe u
54	
55	open TensorProduct
56	
57	namespace Algebra
58	
59	/-- A presented étale cover of `Spec A`: a finite-variable polynomial presentation of an
60	étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum maps onto `Spec A`.  Presentations keep the type of covers
61	small (`Type u` for `A : Type u`), which is what makes the étale plus construction over
62	these covers a legitimate colimit; the carrier-level content is recovered by
63	`Algebra.EtaleCover.of`/`ofEquiv`. -/
64	structure EtaleCover (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : Type u where
65	  /-- The number of variables of the presentation. -/
66	  n : ℕ
67	  /-- The ideal of relations of the presentation. -/
68	  ideal : Ideal (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A)
69	  /-- The presented algebra is étale over the base. -/
70	  etale : Algebra.Etale A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)
71	  /-- The spectrum of the presented algebra covers the spectrum of the base. -/
72	  comap_surjective :
73	    Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ ideal)))
74	
75	namespace EtaleCover
76	
77	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A]
78	
79	/-- The covering algebra presented by an étale cover. -/
80	protected abbrev Carrier (E : EtaleCover A) : Type u :=
81	  MvPolynomial (Fin E.n) A ⧸ E.ideal
82	
83	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Algebra.Etale A E.Carrier :=
84	  E.etale
85	
86	instance (E : EtaleCover A) : Module.FaithfullyFlat A E.Carrier :=
87	  .of_comap_surjective E.comap_surjective
88	
89	/-! ## Constructors -/
90	
91	section constructors
92	
93	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
94	
95	/-- Package an explicitly presented étale algebra with surjective spectrum map as a
96	presented étale cover: the ideal of relations is the kernel of the presenting
97	surjection. -/
98	noncomputable def ofSurjective
99	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
100	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
101	    EtaleCover A where
102	  n := n
103	  ideal := RingHom.ker f
104	  etale := .of_equiv (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).symm
105	  comap_surjective := by
106	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A B := .of_comap_surjective hB
107	    haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (MvPolynomial (Fin n) A ⧸ RingHom.ker f) :=
108	      .of_linearEquiv A B (Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf).toLinearEquiv
109	    exact PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
110	
111	/-- The carrier of `ofSurjective` is the presented algebra. -/
112	noncomputable def ofSurjectiveEquiv
113	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B)))
114	    {n : ℕ} (f : MvPolynomial (Fin n) A →ₐ[A] B) (hf : Function.Surjective f) :
115	    (ofSurjective hB f hf).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
116	  Ideal.quotientKerAlgEquivOfSurjective hf
117	
118	/-- Any étale `A`-algebra whose spectrum covers `Spec A` underlies a presented étale
119	cover.  The presentation is chosen (étale algebras are finitely presented, in particular
120	finitely generated); the choice is harmless because consumers only ever use the carrier
121	identification `ofEquiv`. -/
122	noncomputable def of (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
123	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) : EtaleCover A :=
124	  ofSurjective hB
125	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose
126	    (Algebra.FiniteType.iff_quotient_mvPolynomial''.mp inferInstance).choose_spec.choose_spec
127	
128	/-- The carrier of `of B hB` is `B` itself. -/
129	noncomputable def ofEquiv (B : Type u) [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Algebra.Etale A B]
130	    (hB : Function.Surjective (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A B))) :
131	    (of B hB).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] B :=
132	  ofSurjectiveEquiv hB _ _
133	
134	end constructors
135	
136	/-! ## Refinement and directedness -/
137	
138	/-- `E'` refines `E`: the covering spectrum of `E'` maps to that of `E` over `Spec A`,
139	i.e. there is an `A`-algebra map from the carrier of `E` to that of `E'`.  This is a mere
140	existence: the plus construction proves that the induced maps on descent classes do not
141	depend on the chosen refinement map, so no map is carried here. -/
142	def Refines (E' E : EtaleCover A) : Prop :=
143	  Nonempty (E.Carrier →ₐ[A] E'.Carrier)
144	
145	theorem refines_refl (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines E :=
146	  ⟨AlgHom.id A E.Carrier⟩
147	
148	theorem Refines.trans {E E' E'' : EtaleCover A} (h : E''.Refines E') (h' : E'.Refines E) :
149	    E''.Refines E := by
150	  obtain ⟨f⟩ := h
151	  obtain ⟨g⟩ := h'
152	  exact ⟨f.comp g⟩
153	
154	/-- The common refinement of two covers: `Spec` of the tensor product of the carriers,
155	i.e. the fiber product of the covering spectra over the base. -/
156	noncomputable def prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A :=
157	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
158	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
159	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
160	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
161	  .of (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
162	
163	/-- The carrier of the common refinement is the tensor product of the carriers. -/
164	noncomputable def prodEquiv (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
165	    (E.prod E').Carrier ≃ₐ[A] E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier :=
166	  haveI : Algebra.Etale A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
167	    Algebra.Etale.comp A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
168	  haveI : Module.FaithfullyFlat A (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) :=
169	    Module.FaithfullyFlat.trans A E.Carrier (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier)
170	  ofEquiv (E.Carrier ⊗[A] E'.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
171	
172	/-- The first refinement map of the common refinement. -/
173	noncomputable def prodInl (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
174	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeLeft
175	
176	/-- The second refinement map of the common refinement. -/
177	noncomputable def prodInr (E E' : EtaleCover A) : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.prod E').Carrier :=
178	  ((E.prodEquiv E').symm.toAlgHom).comp Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
179	
180	/-- Combine refinement maps out of the two factors into one out of the common
181	refinement (the universal property of the fiber product of the covering spectra). -/
182	noncomputable def prodLift {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
183	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (E.prod E').Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier :=
184	  (Algebra.TensorProduct.lift f g fun _ _ => Commute.all _ _).comp
185	    (E.prodEquiv E').toAlgHom
186	
187	@[simp]
188	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInl {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
189	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInl E') = f := by
190	  ext x
191	  simp [prodLift, prodInl]
192	
193	@[simp]
194	theorem prodLift_comp_prodInr {E E' F : EtaleCover A} (f : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier)
195	    (g : E'.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) : (prodLift f g).comp (E.prodInr E') = g := by
196	  ext x
197	  simp [prodLift, prodInr]
198	
199	theorem prod_refines_left (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E :=
200	  ⟨E.prodInl E'⟩
201	
202	theorem prod_refines_right (E E' : EtaleCover A) : (E.prod E').Refines E' :=
203	  ⟨E.prodInr E'⟩
204	
205	/-- Directedness of the refinement preorder: any two covers have a common refinement. -/
206	theorem exists_refines_prod (E E' : EtaleCover A) :
207	    ∃ E'' : EtaleCover A, E''.Refines E ∧ E''.Refines E' :=
208	  ⟨E.prod E', E.prod_refines_left E', E.prod_refines_right E'⟩
209	
210	/-- The trivial cover of `Spec A` by itself. -/
211	noncomputable def self (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : EtaleCover A :=
212	  .of A (by
213	    rw [show algebraMap A A = RingHom.id A from rfl, PrimeSpectrum.comap_id]
214	    exact fun p => ⟨p, rfl⟩)
215	
216	/-- The carrier of the trivial cover is the base ring. -/
217	noncomputable def selfEquiv (A : Type u) [CommRing A] : (self A).Carrier ≃ₐ[A] A :=
218	  ofEquiv A _
219	
220	/-- The canonical refinement map from the trivial cover to any cover (algebra side: the
221	structure map of the carrier, through the trivial carrier's identification with `A`). -/
222	noncomputable def fromSelf (E : EtaleCover A) : (self A).Carrier →ₐ[A] E.Carrier :=
223	  (Algebra.ofId A E.Carrier).comp (selfEquiv A).toAlgHom
224	
225	/-- Every cover refines the trivial cover: the trivial cover is the base point of the
226	refinement preorder. -/
227	theorem refines_self (E : EtaleCover A) : E.Refines (self A) :=
228	  ⟨E.fromSelf⟩
229	
230	/-! ## Base change -/
231	
232	section baseChange
233	
234	variable (A' : Type u) [CommRing A'] [Algebra A A']
235	
236	/-- The base change of a cover along `A → A'`: the cover of `Spec A'` with carrier
237	`A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier` (the fiber product of the covering spectrum with the new base). -/
238	noncomputable def baseChange (E : EtaleCover A) : EtaleCover A' :=
239	  .of (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
240	
241	/-- The carrier of the base-changed cover is the base-changed carrier. -/
242	noncomputable def baseChangeEquiv (E : EtaleCover A) :
243	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier ≃ₐ[A'] A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier :=
244	  ofEquiv (A' ⊗[A] E.Carrier) PrimeSpectrum.comap_surjective_of_faithfullyFlat
245	
246	/-- The canonical map from the carrier of a cover to the carrier of its base change,
247	as a map of `A`-algebras. -/
248	noncomputable def baseChangeInclude (E : EtaleCover A) :
249	    E.Carrier →ₐ[A] (E.baseChange A').Carrier :=
250	  (((E.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).restrictScalars A).comp
251	    Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight
252	
253	/-- The base change of a refinement map: `A' ⊗[A] —` on carriers, through the
254	presented-carrier identifications — the functoriality of `baseChange` in the cover. -/
255	noncomputable def baseChangeMap {E F : EtaleCover A} (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
256	    (E.baseChange A').Carrier →ₐ[A'] (F.baseChange A').Carrier :=
257	  ((F.baseChangeEquiv A').symm.toAlgHom).comp
258	    ((Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id A' A') h).comp (E.baseChangeEquiv A').toAlgHom)
259	
260	/-- Base change of refinement maps commutes with the canonical inclusions into the base
261	change. -/
262	theorem baseChangeMap_comp_baseChangeInclude {E F : EtaleCover A}
263	    (h : E.Carrier →ₐ[A] F.Carrier) :
264	    ((baseChangeMap A' h).restrictScalars A).comp (E.baseChangeInclude A')
265	      = (F.baseChangeInclude A').comp h := by
266	  ext x
267	  simp [baseChangeMap, baseChangeInclude]
268	
269	end baseChange
270	
271	/-! ## Covers of a field: single-factor refinement -/
272	
273	section field
274

11	The étale-plus Picard group `PicEtAff C A` is functorial in the affine test: a base

15	base extensions, the extension is carried as instances `[Algebra A A'] [IsScalarTower k A A']`

21	  `relPicAlgMap_congr` applies.

23	  `PicEtAff C A →* PicEtAff C A'`.

27	  any two transports out of the same descent class.

/-!
# Descent of the canonical rank-one divisor from an étale witness

Assuming the rank-one divisor **uniqueness interface** (`RankOneDivisorUniqueness`): over any
affine test whose plus class lies in the rank-one locus, at most one widened divisor class has
that Abel value — the missing-item interface to be discharged by a later session.

Under this hypothesis, a widened divisor over the carrier of an étale cover of the test whose

theorem `DivFamZarAff.exists_descent_of_tensor_eq`, and the Abel value of the descended class
is pinned by étale separatedness of `PicEtAff`.

The first consumer is the finite glue on a Noetherian presentation carrier
(`existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation`), whose Abel conjunct is exactly the
étale witness above.  The unique class is then extracted as the **canonical rank-one divisor**

This is the sanctioned missing-item interface of the canonical-divisor route: producers prove
existence (the finite glue and its descent below), while injectivity of the widened Abel map

assumed: it is manufactured from the uniqueness interface, applied over the tensor square of

restriction of the input class along the (single) structure map `A → E.Carrier ⊗[A] E.Carrier`,

  (existsUnique_abel_divFamZarAff_of_localPresentation pi hu hlam P).choose_spec.1
